meta.title: RDK Course | Lesson 09: RDK S100 Display Module

slides.title: Display Module [gradient]Hands-on HDMI Verification[/gradient]
slides.lead: Complete a repeatable S100 HDMI check from physical wiring and system detection to visible image-quality tests.

slides.title: Build a Complete S100 Verification Loop
slides.lead: The framework is shared, but the board, active mode, and desktop environment need independent evidence.

cards.title: Correct wiring
cards.body: Confirm the S100 HDMI port, cable, monitor, and stable power.

cards.title: System detection
cards.body: DRM and X11 independently report the connector and active mode.

cards.title: Real output
cards.body: Complete color, detail, and motion checks on the physical monitor.

slides.title: Prepare a Stable Recording Setup
slides.lead: This S100 lesson verifies HDMI only; it does not include a DSI workflow.
items: Prepare the S100, HDMI monitor, HDMI cable, and stable power
Select the correct monitor input and keep key ports clearly visible
Enter new_project and run source env.sh
Keep ROS_DOMAIN_ID at 42 and use only ports 9100–9199
Keep the GNOME / X11 desktop awake throughout recording
Keep SSH and VNC enabled; do not change networking or unrelated system projects

steps.title: 1  Check wiring

steps.title: 3  Read status

slides.title: Record the S100 Result Independently
slides.lead: Do not reuse the X5 resolution, desktop stack, or conclusions for the S100.

cards.title: HDMI-1
cards.body: Both DRM and X11 report connected.
Active mode at a 60.00 Hz refresh rate.

cards.title: Eight modes
cards.body: The system lists several candidates, but this lesson does not switch modes.

slides.title: Four Pages Complete the Visible Check

cards.title: Color
cards.body: RGB and CMY boundaries are clear, with no obvious color cast.

cards.title: Grayscale
cards.body: Brightness levels from black to white remain distinguishable.

cards.title: Detail
cards.body: Small Chinese and English text, fine lines, checkerboards, and rings are visible.

cards.title: Motion
cards.body: Motion stays continuous while page rendering remains stable.

slides.title: The Recording Environment Is Part of Success
slides.lead: A lock screen or sleep event is not an HDMI link failure.

steps.body: Disable GNOME idle timeout, automatic dimming, screen lock, and DPMS.
Attach x11vnc to the real :0 session; VNC should match HDMI.
Keep the desktop awake so the camera does not capture a lock screen.
After the demo, confirm SSH, VNC, and the desktop session still work.

slides.title: Six Results Together Define a Pass
slides.lead: The display must look correct, reproduce reliably, and exit without side effects.
items: DRM and X11 both report HDMI-1 as connected
The active mode is 1280×720 at 60.00 Hz
Color, grayscale, text, fine lines, geometry, and motion pages are visible
Ports 9100–9199 are released with no project process left behind
SSH, VNC, and the always-on desktop remain available

slides.title: Separate Signal, Desktop, and Demo Faults

cards.title: No monitor signal
cards.body: Check the input source, cable, and power before reading DRM status.

cards.title: Screen turns black
cards.body: Check screen lock, sleep, and DPMS before changing HDMI settings.

cards.title: Black VNC view
cards.body: Confirm VNC uses the real X11 session and the correct Xauthority.

cards.title: Demo fails
cards.body: Inspect terminal safety checks, runtime.json, and server.log.

slides.title: The S100 HDMI Verification Loop Is Complete
slides.lead: Remember the board-specific result, three evidence layers, and six pass criteria. This video does not include DSI.

cards.title: Confirm resolution
cards.body: Compare the monitor menu with the active xrandr mode.

cards.title: Run it again
cards.body: Start from a clean state, repeat the demo, and complete cleanup.
